name: Chongoni Rock-Art Area
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2006.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “Situated within a cluster of forested granite hills and covering an area of 126.4 km2, high up the plateau of central Malawi, the 127 sites of this area feature the richest concentration of rock art in Central Africa. They reflect the comparatively scarce tradition of farmer rock art, as well as paintings by BaTwa hunter-gatherers who inhabited the area from the late Stone Age. The Chewa agriculturalists, whose ancestors lived there from the late Iron Age, practised rock painting until well into the 20th century. The symbols in the rock art, which are strongly associated with women, still have cultural relevance amongst the Chewa, and the sites are actively associated with ceremonies and rituals.”
The Chongoni area holds 127 rock art sites in the forested hills of the Malawi plateau, in the Central Region, according to Wikipedia.

It attributes the art to two groups: the BaTwa hunter-gatherers of the Stone Age and the Chewa farmers of the Iron Age, with the later paintings mostly made by Chewa women and linked to rituals and ceremonies.
The area is near Dedza, the highest town in Malawi, about 80 kilometres south-east of Lilongwe.

gaps: Chewa voices on the paintings and their continuing ritual use, which UNESCO's criterion vi points to but which the article only touches.
Dating of the paintings, which the part of the article read here does not give.
